title: Relative Tor amplitude and its module criterion on an affine scheme
statement: Let $R\to A$ be any homomorphism of commutative rings and $f:U=\operatorname{Spec}A\to V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ its scheme morphism [def-pc-scheme]. Let $M^\bullet$ be a complex of $A$-modules and $E=\widetilde{M^\bullet}\in D(\mathcal O_U)$ its termwise associated-sheaf object [def-pc-derived-category], [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence]. Regard $E$ as an object of $D(f^{-1}\mathcal O_V)$ by restriction of scalars. For integers $a\le b$, the following are equivalent: (1) $H^i(E\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{f^{-1}\mathcal O_V}\mathcal F)=0$ for every $f^{-1}\mathcal O_V$-module sheaf $\mathcal F$ and every $i\notin[a,b]$; (2) $H^i(M^\bullet\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N)=0$ for every $R$-module $N$ in degree zero and every $i\notin[a,b]$. In (1) it is equivalent to test only sheaves $\mathcal F=f^{-1}\mathcal G$ for $\mathcal O_V$-module sheaves $\mathcal G$. Moreover, $E$ locally has finite Tor dimension over $f^{-1}\mathcal O_V$ (each point has an open neighbourhood on which (1) holds for some finite interval) if and only if $M^\bullet$ has finite Tor amplitude over $R$ (condition (2) for one finite interval). The derived tensors are computed by K-flat resolutions, as in [def-pc-finite-tor-dimension-over]; no flatness, finite-presentation, boundedness or Noetherian hypothesis on $R\to A$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0DHY, lemma-tor-dimension-rel-affine, clauses (1) and (2); the inverse-image-test formulation is the equivalent stalk test (any module over O_{V,v} is the stalk of its direct image from the one-point ringed space v).

proof.text: Put $\mathcal B=f^{-1}\mathcal O_V$ and $C=\operatorname{Res}_{\mathcal B}\widetilde M$. By [lem-trf-affine-relative-stalk-resolution-iso], its stalk at $\mathfrak q$ over $\mathfrak p$ is $Q(M_{\mathfrak q})$ in $D(R_{\mathfrak p})$, with the actual scheme scalar map. By [lem-trf-ringed-tor-amplitude-stalk-test], (1) is therefore equivalent to amplitude $[a,b]$ of all these localized complexes. This is exactly (2) by [lem-trf-relative-tor-amplitude-localization].

source.place: Tag 0DHY, lemma-tor-dimension-rel-affine, proof of (1); algebraic criterion Tag 0B67.

proof.text: All-sheaf testing implies inverse-image testing. Conversely fix $\mathfrak q$ over $\mathfrak p$ and any $R_{\mathfrak p}$-module $L$. The base skyscraper $\mathcal G=i_{f(\mathfrak q),*}L$ is an allowed base sheaf. By [lem-trf-affine-base-skyscraper-tensor-cohomology], the stalk of the assumed vanishing against $f^{-1}\mathcal G$ is $H^i(M_{\mathfrak q}\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{R_{\mathfrak p}}L)$. Thus every localized test vanishes outside $[a,b]$, and Step 1 gives (1).

source.place: Tag 0DHY with the skyscraper realization in its expanded stalk argument.

proof.text: The underlying space $U$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Apply conditions (3)$\Longleftrightarrow$(4) of [lem-trf-ringed-tor-amplitude-stalk-test] to $(U,\mathcal B)$ and $C$: local finite relative Tor dimension is equivalent to one global finite interval in (1). Step 1 identifies existence of such an interval with finite $R$-Tor amplitude of $M$. The cited ringed-space statement includes the empty-space case. This proves both directions of the final assertion.
For $M=0$ every interval works. For $R=A$ these identifications give the absolute affine criterion. The cited inputs impose no flatness, finite presentation, boundedness or Noetherian assumption.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0DHY, lemma-tor-dimension-rel-affine; the cited stalk proof is expanded using cohomology.tex Tag 09U9, and the inverse-image-test addendum is proved by skyscraper tests.

lean.statement: theorem affine_relative_torAmplitude_iff {R A : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing A] (φ : R →+* A) [HasDerivedCategory.{wR} (ModuleCat.{u} R)] (M : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ) (a b : ℤ) (_hab : a ≤ b) : (∀ (F : SheafOfModules.{u} ((sheafCompose (Opens.grothendieckTopology (Spec (.of A))) (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj (TopCat.Sheaf.inverseImageRing (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ)).base (Spec (.of R)).sheaf))) (i : ℤ), i < a ∨ b < i → CochainComplex.sheafDerivedTensorVanishes (TopCat.Sheaf.inverseImageRing (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ)).base (Spec (.of R)).sheaf) (affineRelativeTorComplex φ M) F i) ↔ DerivedCategory.torAmplitudeIn (ModuleCat.{u} R) a b (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (((ModuleCat.restrictScalars φ).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj M))
